analysis:
Examined all supplied ProviderLoop.swift excerpts, DaemonState+Coding.swift metadata and patch against the canonical index and detailed T-041 definition. The complete range map limits ProviderLoop changes to head lines 484–497: actor-owned add-on hold bookkeeping, driver/monitor tasks, generation, local IPC server/path references, and authentication/time/drain test seams. DaemonState+Coding.swift head lines 18, 56 and 93 add optional AddonHoldSnapshot decoding/encoding. These declarations and serialization changes alone establish neither an authorization bypass nor a disclosure. No supported regression was identified in the supplied scope; unchanged key generation, attestation state, model identity, cache eligibility and transport code were distinguished from the additions.
Integration must examine ProviderLoop+AddonHold and AddonIPCServer wiring: peer authentication and socket ownership under TB-003, bounded lease renewal and hold-history growth, generation-safe task cleanup, shutdown cancellation, and admission/drain/unload interaction with local reservations, model loads, updates and reconnects (TB-007, T-010, T-029, T-053). Verify that an add-on hold cannot reopen serving authorization or release resources still owned by inference, and assess whether the local IPC contract requires threat-model coverage. Authentication overrides shown at ProviderLoop.swift:493–497 are internal seams, not proof of a production bypass. Inspect AddonHoldSnapshot and daemon-state consumers for sensitive identifiers or attacker-controlled diagnostics (A-001, A-008, T-058); optional coding itself supplies no evidence of a leak. Cache teardown must preserve T-041 encryption and scope bindings if the hold driver touches cache resources. These implementations are outside this batch, so the new local control boundary remains unresolved rather than an observed missing control.
